title: An Influence Graph Over AI Agents Certifies an Agent That Copies Nobody
abstract: Circular-shift surrogates can produce severely inflated false-positive rates when applied to turn-ordered multi-agent conversations, reaching a family-wise error rate of 0.90 against a nominal 0.05. A generated benchmark separates two candidate mechanisms and points at non-stationary speaker activity rather than turn-taking, which suppresses the failure rather than causing it. No setting of either knob reproduces the observed 0.90, however, so what drives the full real-data failure remains open. Restricted permutation surrogates substantially reduce the problem. Their error rate is flat with respect to drift rather than at the nominal level, and for the global within-speaker variant it depends on how many surrogate draws the null is built from. Calibration alone does not address confounding, which motivates a conditional estimator validated against a benchmark with planted ground truth. I also identify a symbolisation-dependent detection limit and develop label-free diagnostics for it, and show that their calibration does not transport across degradation mechanisms. The benchmark is released.
